articleTitle: How major fitness apps use hidden recurring billing clauses and dark pattern cancellation flows to b
summary: How major fitness apps use hidden recurring billing clauses and dark pattern cancellation flows to bill former members for years.

systemMechanisms.plainEnglish: The consumer believes they are testing a service or making a small purchase, not authorizing an open-ended payment relationship.
systemMechanisms.evidence: Noom’s complaint challenged risk-free trial messaging; the FTC challenged free or low, one-time-cost messaging in the Genesis Tech enterprise.​

systemMechanisms.mechanism: Separate the prominent promise from the billing terms
systemMechanisms.plainEnglish: The attractive offer receives attention while the recurring obligation is harder to notice.
systemMechanisms.evidence: The FTC alleged renewal references appeared in the smallest print. Beachbody’s injunction required separate renewal consent rather than consent bundled with other terms.​

systemMechanisms.mechanism: Convert the trial without a fresh purchase decision
systemMechanisms.plainEnglish: The deadline passes and the payment system proceeds unless the customer has completed cancellation.
systemMechanisms.evidence: The Noom complaint alleged automatic conversion even for consumers who never accessed the service or downloaded the app.

systemMechanisms.plainEnglish: Missing the cancellation window can produce a substantial immediate charge rather than a small monthly payment.
systemMechanisms.evidence: The original Noom complaint coverage described a non-refundable advance charge of as much as $199.99 for six months.

systemMechanisms.mechanism: Make the exit harder than the entrance
systemMechanisms.plainEnglish: Joining on a website does not necessarily provide an equally straightforward website exit.
systemMechanisms.evidence: The historical Noom complaint described a smartphone-and-coach cancellation route. The FTC alleged missing cancellation controls and mandatory explanations in the Genesis Tech enterprise.​

systemMechanisms.plainEnglish: A customer can stop exercising, logging in, or engaging while the payment relationship continues.
systemMechanisms.evidence: Noom’s settlement specifically required disabling autorenewal for class users inactive throughout the first twelve (12) months after their trial.
systemMechanisms.qualification: That remedy does not establish that every inactive user was charged for years.

systemMechanisms.mechanism: Fail to honor a completed exit
systemMechanisms.plainEnglish: The most serious alleged version is not confusion about how to cancel: the company confirms cancellation but still charges or attempts to charge.
systemMechanisms.evidence: The FTC expressly alleged this conduct against the Genesis Tech enterprise.

systemMechanisms.plainEnglish: Changing corporate identities and merchant accounts can make it harder for fraud controls to connect recurring problems to the same operator.
systemMechanisms.evidence: The FTC alleged repeated creation of companies and merchant accounts to evade fraud monitoring. This allegation should not be transferred to Noom or Beachbody.

coreControversy.criticismOrAlarm: Unregulated shadow banking float without FDIC protection
coreControversy.regulatoryOrHistoricalPrecedent: Exempt from reserve ratios and Dodd-Frank requirements
